contract.words: Collect $3,000 of settled cash within 14 days with at most $200 of capital.

terms.proofCondition: At least $3,000 of settled cash received within 14 days, with no more than $200 of capital committed.

strategy.title: Deliver the three signed FAA Part 137 audit packs and collect $3,600 by day 10
strategy.why: Three operators signed engagement letters at $1,200 each (EVIDENCE: signed Nov 24-26). Brain produces the pack (PRODUCE_SPREADSHEET proved) and delivers all three by Dec 1; each pays net 7 from delivery, so $3,600 settles by Dec 8 (day 10) of a 14-day window, $600 above the $3,000 target. The only outlay is the $25 records-retrieval fee per operator paid up front: $75 in total (the card's exposure fact is $75, and offerScope says $25 per operator), well inside the $200 capital limit. I disagree with Brain's NOT_VIABLE reading: it treats the opening's $75 peak funding as a per-deal figure (3 x $75 = $225 > $200), but the card's own record states the fee is $25 per operator and the total exposure is $75, so all three packs fit inside $200 at once and no deadline relaxation is needed.

brain.summary: INFEASIBLE AS STATED: inside the goal's own limits the openings held bring at most $2,400 of the $3,000 still needed, even with every buyer agreeing at the top price. To make it supportable, capital: allow the goal to commit at least $225, what the lots that reach the target need at once; or deadline: move the deadline to at least 20 days from now, when enough lots have settled; or target: lower the target to about $2,400, the most the openings held bring with every buyer agreeing at the top price. The conclusion covers the openings held; markets nobody has counted are not ruled out, so Brain keeps searching for openings outside them.

reviews.reasons: EXECUTABLE is supported and the author's disagreement with Brain's NOT_VIABLE reading is correct. Three operators signed engagement letters at $1,200 per audit pack (price fact EVIDENCE, three WRITTEN_ACCEPTANCE agreements), so no new deals, conversion or market volume is needed. Fulfilment is Brain's (PRODUCE_SPREADSHEET proved, delivery a spreadsheet Brain produces). Capital: the card's offerScope says a $25 records-retrieval fee per operator is paid up front and the exposure fact is $75 total, i.e. 3 x $25; Brain's planner treated peakFundingCents 7500 as per-lot (3 x $75 = $225 > $200), which double-counts the same $75. Recomputed: peak capital $75 <= $200 cap; 3 x $1,200 = $3,600 >= $3,000; delivery of all three by Dec 1 (day 3) plus net 7 = Dec 8 (day 10) of 14; net $3,525. Ledger (three $25 spends day 0, three $1,200 receipts settling day 10) matches the steps and the trace (max exposure $75, $3,600 collected in window).
findings: Recomputed: 3 x $1,200 = $3,600 gross, $75 up-front fees, $3,525 net; settles day 10 of 14; peak capital $75 of the $200 cap.

Brain's NOT_VIABLE verdict rests on reading peakFundingCents $75 as per deal; the card's own facts (offerScope '$25 per operator', exposure '$75', directCosts '$25') show $75 is the total for all three.
Residual risk: settlement depends on each operator paying on net-7 terms as signed; only 4 days of slack (day 10 vs 14) if a payment is late. No deposit is taken.
The plan needs each operator's records to compile the pack; the sell step requests them on day 0, so delivery by Dec 1 assumes the records arrive promptly.
Operational note: ISSUE_AN_INVOICE and SEND_A_MESSAGE are NOT_CONNECTED; invoicing must be connected before day 3.
